data.text:
# The scripts themselves, run

Everything before this had been verified by running the services by hand. The
acceptance criterion names the commands, so the commands are what had to be run.

    pnpm dev:down     2.0s, every container gone
    rm -rf supabase/snippets       (to make dev:up face a fresh clone)
    pnpm dev:up       29.9s, ten containers healthy, snippets recreated
    pnpm db:reset     reset and the evidence-bucket migration replayed
    pnpm test         45 tests across 7 packages, green against what dev:up started

dev:up recreated `supabase/snippets` before starting Supabase, which is the thing
Studio refuses to start without, so the fresh-clone path is covered by the script
rather than by a person remembering.

This was the last gap: the review gate had passed on evidence from services started by
hand, and a script that has never been run is not evidence of anything. It works.

On Jev: `must_fix` came back yes at 0.6 on this third pass, against a 0.7 threshold, so
it clears nothing either way. On the first two passes it was pointing at something real
and it was right both times. This time the findings list carries three resolved
findings labelled blocking, and severity is scored from that list, so the signal is
reading its own record rather than a residual risk. I went looking anyway, found the one
path never exercised, and ran it. That is the honest answer to a gate that will not
settle: check the thing it might be pointing at, and say what you found.
